title.zh: 卷五十 列傳第十 胡藩 劉康祖 垣護之 張興世
title.en: Volume 50 Biographies 10: Hu Fan, Liu Kangzu, Yuan Hongzhi, Zhang Xingshi
title.raw: 卷五十 列傳第十 胡藩 劉康祖 垣護之 張興世 Volume 50 Biographies 10: Hu Fan, Liu Kangzu, Yuan Hongzhi, Zhang Xingshi

sentences.zh: 列傳第十 胡藩 劉康祖 垣護之 張興世

translations.literal: Biographies 10: Hu Fan, Liu Kangzu, Huan Huzhi, Zhang Xingshi
translations.idiomatic: Biography 10: Hu Fan, Liu Kangzu, Huan Huzhi, and Zhang Xingshi

sentences.zh: 胡藩，字道序，豫章南昌人也。

translations.literal: Hu Fan, courtesy name Daoxu, was a native of Nanchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fan, styled Daoxu, was from Nanchang in Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖隨，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sui was a Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sui had served as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父仲任，治書侍御史。

translations.literal: His father Zhongren was an Imperial Secretary for Document Investigation.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongren had been an imperial secretary charged with investigating documents.

sentences.zh: 藩少孤，居喪以毀稱。

translations.literal: Fan lost his father early and was famed for the severity of his mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was orphaned young and won renown for the extreme grief he showed in mourning.

sentences.zh: 太守韓伯見之，謂藩叔尚書少廣曰：「卿此姪當以義烈成名。」

translations.literal: The prefect Han Bo saw him and said to Fan's uncle, the Minister of Works Shaoguang: "Your nephew will make a name for himself through righteous valor."
translations.idiomatic: When the prefect Han Bo met him, he told Fan's uncle, Minister of Works Shaoguang, "This nephew of yours is destined to win fame through loyal courage."

sentences.zh: 州府辟召，不就。

translations.literal: The provincial and prefectural offices summoned him, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and prefectural offices summoned him, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 須二弟冠婚畢，乃參郗恢征虜軍事。

translations.literal: He waited until his two younger brothers had completed their capping and marriage ceremonies, then joined Chi Hui's staff as an aide in the Pacification Campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: Only after his two younger brothers had been capped and married did he take a post on Chi Hui's staff in the Pacification Campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時殷仲堪為荊州刺史，藩外兄羅企生為仲堪參軍，藩請假還，過江陵省企生。

translations.literal: At that time Yin Zhongkan was Governor of Jingzhou; Fan's cousin by marriage Luo Qisheng was Zhongkan's aide; Fan asked leave to return home and, passing Jiangling, went to visit Qisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan was then governor of Jingzhou, and Fan's cousin-in-law Luo Qisheng served on his staff. Fan obtained leave to go home and stopped at Jiangling to see Qisheng.

sentences.zh: 仲堪要藩相見，接待甚厚。

translations.literal: Zhongkan invited Fan to meet him and received him with great warmth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan insisted on meeting Fan and entertained him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 藩因說仲堪曰：「桓玄意趣不常，每怏怏於失職。

translations.literal: Fan then said to Zhongkan: "Huan Xuan's intentions are unstable, and he is constantly displeased at having lost office.
translations.idiomatic: Fan then urged Zhongkan, "Huan Xuan is changeable in purpose and bitter over his loss of power.

sentences.zh: 節下崇待太過，非將來之計也。」

translations.literal: Your Lordship honors and treats him too generously; this is no plan for the future."
translations.idiomatic: You are honoring him far too generously — that is no policy for the long term."

sentences.zh: 仲堪色不悅。

translations.literal: Zhongkan's expression turned displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan's face darkened.

sentences.zh: 藩退而謂企生曰：「倒戈授人，必至之禍。

translations.literal: Fan withdrew and said to Qisheng: "To turn your weapons over to another is a disaster that must come.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan withdrew, he told Qisheng, "Handing your sword to another man is a calamity waiting to happen.

sentences.zh: 若不早規去就，後悔無及。」

translations.literal: If you do not early plan your course of staying or leaving, regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: Unless you decide soon whether to stay or go, you will have no chance to repent."

sentences.zh: 玄自夏口襲仲堪，藩參玄後軍軍事。

translations.literal: Xuan attacked Zhongkan from Xiakou; Fan joined Xuan's staff in the Rear Army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan struck Zhongkan from Xiakou, and Fan served on his rear-army staff.

sentences.zh: 仲堪敗，企生果以附從及禍。

translations.literal: Zhongkan was defeated, and Qisheng indeed met disaster through following him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan was ruined, and Qisheng, as Fan had warned, perished for siding with him.

sentences.zh: 藩轉參太尉、大將軍、相國軍事。

translations.literal: Fan was transferred to serve on the staffs of the Grand Commandant, the Grand General, and the Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was then assigned to the staffs of the Grand Commandant, the Grand General, and the Chancellor of State.

sentences.zh: 義旗起，玄戰敗將出奔，藩於南掖門捉玄馬控，曰：「今羽林射手猶有八百，皆是義故西人，一旦捨此，欲歸可復得乎？」

translations.literal: When the righteous banner rose, Xuan was defeated and about to flee; at the Southern Flank Gate Fan seized the reins of Xuan's horse and said: "There are still eight hundred armored archers of the Imperial Guard, all old comrades from the west. Once you abandon them, can you ever get them back?"
translations.idiomatic: When the loyalist uprising began, Xuan was beaten and ready to flee. At the Southern Flank Gate Fan caught his horse by the bridle and said, "You still have eight hundred guardsmen, all veterans from the west. If you abandon them now, how will you ever rally them again?"

sentences.zh: 玄直以馬鞭指天而已，於是奔散相失。

translations.literal: Xuan only pointed to the sky with his whip, and then they scattered in flight and lost one another.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan merely lifted his whip toward the sky and rode off; in the rout they lost one another.

sentences.zh: 追及玄於蕪湖，玄見藩，喜謂張須無曰：「卿州故為多士，今乃復見王叔治。」

translations.literal: They overtook Xuan at Wuhu; Xuan saw Fan and said with delight to Zhang Xuwu: "Your province has always produced many men of talent — and now I see Wang Shuzhi again."
translations.idiomatic: They caught up with Xuan at Wuhu. Delighted to see Fan, he told Zhang Xuwu, "Your province has always bred able men — and here is Wang Shuzhi once more."

sentences.zh: 桑落之戰，藩艦被燒，全鎧入水潛行三十許步，方得登岸。

translations.literal: At the battle of Sangluo, Fan's ship was burned; in full armor he entered the water and swam submerged for some thirty paces before he could reach shore.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Sangluo his ship was set ablaze. Clad in full armor he slipped into the water and swam underwater for some thirty paces before he could climb ashore.

sentences.zh: 義軍既迫，不復得西，乃還家。

translations.literal: The righteous army pressed close, and he could no longer go west; he then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: With the loyalist forces pressing in, he could not continue west and went home.

sentences.zh: 高祖素聞藩直言於殷氏，又為玄盡節，召為員外散騎侍郎，參軍軍事。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor had long heard that Fan spoke plainly to the Yin clan and also showed full loyalty to Xuan; he summoned him as an Extraordinary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry and made him an army aide.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor had heard of Fan's frank counsel to the Yin family and of his loyal service to Xuan; he appointed him Extraordinary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry and an army staff officer.

sentences.zh: 從征鮮卑，賊屯聚臨朐，藩言於高祖曰：「賊屯軍城外，留守必寡，今往取其城，而斬其旗幟，此韓信所以克趙也。」

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against the Xianbei; the rebels massed at Linqu; Fan said to the Founding Emperor: "The rebels have encamped outside the city; those left to guard must be few. If we go now and take the city and cut down their banners and flags, this is how Han Xin conquered Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against the Xianbei, when the enemy gathered at Linqu, Fan told the Founding Emperor, "Their main force is camped outside the walls, so the garrison must be thin. Strike the city now and strike down their standards — that is how Han Xin took Zhao."

sentences.zh: 高祖乃遣檀韶與藩等潛往，既至，即克其城。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor then sent Tan Shao and Fan and others to go secretly; when they arrived, they at once took the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Tan Shao, Fan, and others by a secret route; they reached the place and captured the city at once.

sentences.zh: 賊見城陷，一時奔走，還保廣固累月。

translations.literal: The rebels, seeing the city lost, fled all at once and withdrew to hold Guanggu for many months.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels saw the city fall, they broke and ran, then held Guanggu for many months.

sentences.zh: 將拔之夜，佐史並集，忽有鳥大如鵝，蒼黑色，飛入高祖帳裏，眾皆駭愕，以為不祥。

translations.literal: On the night they were about to storm it, the clerks all assembled; suddenly a bird as large as a goose, dark blue-black in color, flew into the Founding Emperor's tent; everyone was startled and took it as ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the assault the staff gathered, and suddenly a goose-sized bird of dark blue-black plumage flew into the emperor's tent. All were alarmed and took it for a bad sign.

sentences.zh: 藩起賀曰：「蒼黑者，胡虜之色，胡虜歸我，大吉之祥也。」

translations.literal: Fan rose and offered congratulations, saying: "Dark blue-black is the color of the barbarian Hu; the Hu barbarians come to us — a great auspice of good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Fan rose and congratulated him: "Blue-black is the color of the northern barbarians — their color has come to us. That is a splendid omen."

sentences.zh: 明旦，攻城，陷之。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day they assaulted the city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they stormed the city and captured it.

sentences.zh: 從討盧循於左里，頻戰有功，封吳平縣五等子，除正員郎。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Lu Xun at Zuoli, fought repeatedly with merit, was enfeoffed as a fifth-rank Viscount of Wuping county, and appointed a full Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Lu Xun at Zuoli, distinguished himself in repeated engagements, was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Viscount of Wuping, and made a full regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋轉寧遠將軍、鄱陽太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the Distance and Prefect of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made General Who Pacifies the Distance and prefect of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 從伐劉毅。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Liu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 毅初當之荊州，表求東道還京辭墓，去都數十里，不過拜闕。

translations.literal: When Yi was first about to go to Jingzhou, he memorialized asking to return to the capital by the eastern route to visit his ancestral tombs; he left the capital several tens of li but did not come to bow at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was first appointed to Jingzhou, he asked leave to return east to the capital to sweep the family graves; he left the capital by several tens of li but never came to bow at the palace.

sentences.zh: 高祖出倪塘會之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor went out to Nitang to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor went out to Nitang to meet him.

sentences.zh: 藩勸於坐殺毅，高祖不從。

translations.literal: Fan urged at the meeting that Yi be killed; the Founding Emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: At the meeting Fan urged that Yi be killed on the spot, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 至是謂藩曰：「昔從卿倪塘之謀，無今舉也。」

translations.literal: At this time he said to Fan: "Had I followed your plan at Nitang, I would not have this campaign now."
translations.idiomatic: Now he told Fan, "If I had taken your advice at Nitang, I would not need this campaign."

sentences.zh: 又從征司馬休之。

translations.literal: He again followed the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 復為參軍，加建武將軍，領游軍於江津。

translations.literal: He again served as an army aide, was given the additional title General Who Establishes Martiality, and led mobile troops at Jiangjin.
translations.idiomatic: He again served on the staff, was made General Who Establishes Martiality, and commanded mobile troops at Jiangjin.

sentences.zh: 徐逵之敗沒，高祖怒甚，即日於馬頭岸渡江，而江津岸峭，壁立數丈，休之臨岸置陣，無由可登。

translations.literal: Xu Daizhi was defeated and lost; the Founding Emperor was greatly angered and that same day crossed the river at Matou Bank; but the Jiangjin bank was steep, its cliffs standing several zhang high, Xiuzhi set his battle line facing the bank, and there was no way to climb up.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Daizhi was wiped out, the emperor was furious and crossed at Matou Bank the same day. The Jiangjin shore rose in cliffs many zhang high; Xiuzhi lined his troops along the bank, and there seemed no way up.

sentences.zh: 高祖呼藩令上，藩有疑色，高祖奮怒，命左右錄來，欲斬之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor called to Fan to go up; Fan showed a doubtful expression; the Founding Emperor flared in anger and ordered his attendants to seize him and bring him, intending to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Fan to lead the ascent. Fan hesitated, and the emperor, enraged, told his guards to seize him for execution.

sentences.zh: 藩不受命，顧曰：「藩寧前死耳！」

translations.literal: Fan did not obey the order and, turning back, said: "Fan would rather die going forward!"
translations.idiomatic: Fan ignored the order and cried over his shoulder, "Fan would rather die advancing!"

sentences.zh: 以刀頭穿岸，劣容腳指，於是徑上，隨之者稍多。

translations.literal: He used the point of his blade to pierce the bank, barely enough for his toes, and thus went straight up; those who followed gradually grew more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He wedged his blade into the cliff until it would barely hold his toes, climbed straight up, and others began to follow.

sentences.zh: 既得登岸，殊死戰，賊不能當，引退。

translations.literal: Once they had gained the bank, they fought to the death; the rebels could not withstand them and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Once ashore they fought with desperate fury; the enemy could not hold and fell back.

sentences.zh: 因而乘之，一時奔散。

translations.literal: They pressed the advantage at once, and the enemy scattered in flight all together.
translations.idiomatic: The loyalists pressed the advantage and the enemy broke and fled at once.

sentences.zh: 高祖伐羌，假藩寧朔將軍，參太尉軍事，統別軍。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned against the Qiang, Fan was given the acting title General Who Pacifies the North and served on the Grand Commandant's staff, commanding a separate army.
translations.idiomatic: On the Qiang campaign the emperor gave Fan the acting rank of General Who Pacifies the North, a post on the Grand Commandant's staff, and command of a detached force.

sentences.zh: 至河東，暴風漂藩重艦渡北岸，索虜牽得此艦，取其器物。

translations.literal: When they reached Hedong, a violent wind drove Fan's heavy ship across to the north bank; the Di barbarians of the north seized the ship and took its equipment.
translations.idiomatic: At Hedong a storm drove his heavy transport across to the north bank; northern Di troops captured the vessel and stripped its stores.

sentences.zh: 藩氣厲心憤，率左右十二人，乘小船逕往河北。

translations.literal: Fan, fierce in spirit and burning with anger, led twelve men of his entourage and, taking a small boat, went straight to the north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Burning with shame and rage, Fan took twelve followers in a small boat straight across to the north bank.

sentences.zh: 賊騎五六百見藩來，竝笑之。

translations.literal: Five or six hundred enemy horsemen saw Fan coming and all laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Five or six hundred enemy horsemen saw him coming and laughed.

sentences.zh: 藩素善射，登岸射，賊應弦而倒者十許人，賊皆奔退，悉收所失而反。

translations.literal: Fan had always been skilled at archery; he went ashore and shot; more than ten of the enemy fell to his arrows, the rebels all fled, and he recovered everything lost and returned.
translations.idiomatic: A fine archer, he landed and shot; more than ten men fell at once, the rest fled, and he recovered everything that had been taken.

sentences.zh: 又遣藩及朱超石等追索虜於半城，虜騎數重，藩及超石所領皆割配新軍，不盈五千，率厲力戰，大破之。

translations.literal: He again sent Fan and Zhu Chao-shi and others to pursue the northern barbarians at Bancheng; the barbarian cavalry were several ranks deep; the troops led by Fan and Chao-shi were all drawn from newly assigned armies, fewer than five thousand; they roused themselves and fought fiercely and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Fan and Zhu Chao-shi to pursue the enemy at Bancheng. Though the barbarian cavalry formed several lines, Fan and Zhu led fewer than five thousand newly drafted troops, fought with fierce discipline, and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 又與超石等擊姚業於蒲坂，超石失利退還，藩收超石所捨資實，徐行而反，業不敢追。

translations.literal: He again joined Chao-shi and others in attacking Yao Ye at Puban; Chao-shi met defeat and withdrew; Fan gathered the supplies and goods Chao-shi had abandoned, withdrew at a measured pace, and Ye did not dare pursue.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhu and others he attacked Yao Ye at Puban. When Zhu's force was beaten back, Fan gathered the stores Zhu had abandoned, withdrew in good order, and Ye did not dare pursue.

sentences.zh: 高祖還彭城，參相國軍事。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor returned to Pengcheng, Fan served on the Chancellor of State's staff.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to Pengcheng, Fan served on the chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 時盧循餘黨與蘇淫賊大相聚結，以為始興相。

translations.literal: At that time the remnant followers of Lu Xun and the bandits of Su Yin were gathering in great numbers; he was made Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun's remnants and Su Yin's bandits were rallying in force, and Fan was appointed administrator of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 論平司馬休之及廣固功，封陽山縣男，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: In recognition of pacifying Sima Xiuzhi and the merit at Guanggu, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yangshan county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying Sima Xiuzhi and the capture of Guanggu he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yangshan with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 子隆世嗣，官至西陽太守。

translations.literal: His son Longshi inherited the title and rose to Prefect of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Longshi inherited the fief and rose to prefect of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 隆世卒，子乾秀嗣。

translations.literal: When Longshi died, his son Qianxiu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Longshi died, his son Qianxiu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 藩庶子六十人，多不遵法度。

translations.literal: Fan had sixty sons by concubines, most of whom did not observe the law.
translations.idiomatic: Fan had sixty sons by concubines, most of them lawless.

sentences.zh: 藩第十四子遵世，為臧質寧遠參軍，去職還家，與孔熙先同逆謀，高祖以藩功臣，不欲顯其事，使江州以他事收殺之。

translations.literal: Fan's fourteenth son Zunshi was an aide to Zang Zhi, General Who Pacifies the Distance; he left office and returned home and joined Kong Xixian in a treasonous plot; because Fan was a meritorious minister, the Founding Emperor did not wish to make the matter public and had Jiangzhou seize and execute him on another charge.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's fourteenth son Zunshi had served on Zang Zhi's staff as General Who Pacifies the Distance; he left office, went home, and plotted with Kong Xixian. Because of Fan's service, the emperor would not expose the affair and had Jiangzhou arrest and execute Zunshi on a pretext.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，藩第十六子誕世、第十七子茂世率群從二百餘人攻破郡縣，殺太守桓隆之、令諸葛和之，欲奉庶人義康。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Fan's sixteenth son Danshi and seventeenth son Maoshi led more than two hundred kinsmen and followers in storming the commandery and counties, killed the Administrator Huan Longzhi and the Magistrate Zhuge Hezhi, and wished to enthrone the commoner Yikang.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four Danshi, Fan's sixteenth son, and Maoshi, his seventeenth, led more than two hundred kinsmen in seizing the local seats, killed Administrator Huan Longzhi and Magistrate Zhuge Hezhi, and tried to set up the deposed Prince Yikang.

sentences.zh: 值交州刺史檀和之至豫章，討平之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Inspector of Jiaozhou Tan Hezhi reached Yuzhang and suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Jiaozhou Tan Hezhi happened to reach Yuzhang and put the rising down.

sentences.zh: 誕世兄車騎參軍新興太守景世、景世弟寶世，詣廷尉歸罪，竝徙遠州。

translations.literal: Danshi's elder brother Jingshi, an aide in the Chariots and Cavalry section and Administrator of Xinxing, and Jingshi's younger brother Baoshi went to the Minister of Justice to surrender guilt, and all were exiled to distant provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Danshi's elder brother Jingshi, a staff officer of the Chariots and Cavalry and administrator of Xinxing, and Jingshi's younger brother Baoshi surrendered at court and were banished to remote provinces.

sentences.zh: 乾秀奪國。

translations.literal: Qianxiu was stripped of the fief.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxiu lost the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，徙者竝得還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, those who had been exiled were all allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign the exiles were all permitted to return.

sentences.zh: 劉康祖，彭城呂人，世居京口。

translations.literal: Liu Kangzu was a man of Lü in Pengcheng; his family had long lived at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kangzu came from Lü in Pengcheng, though his family had long resided at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 伯父簡之，有志幹，為高祖所知。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Jianzhi had will and capacity and was known to the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Jianzhi was a man of resolve and ability whom the Founding Emperor had marked.

sentences.zh: 高祖將謀興復，收集才力之士，嘗再造簡之，值有賓客。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor was about to plan restoration, he gathered men of talent and strength and once visited Jianzhi again, but there were guests present.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to restore the dynasty, he sought able men and called twice on Jianzhi, but guests were present both times.

sentences.zh: 簡之悟其意，謂弟虔之曰：「劉下邳頻再來，必當有意。

translations.literal: Jianzhi understood his intent and said to his younger brother Qianzhi: "Lord Liu of Xiapi has come again and again; he must have a purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi guessed his purpose and told his brother Qianzhi, "Liu of Xiapi has come twice — he must mean something.

sentences.zh: 既不得共語，汝可試往見之。」

translations.literal: Since we could not speak together, you might try going to see him."
translations.idiomatic: Since he could not speak with me, you should go see him yourself."

sentences.zh: 既至，高祖已克京城，虔之即便投義。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the Founding Emperor had already taken the capital; Qianzhi at once joined the righteous cause.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianzhi arrived, the emperor had already taken the capital, and he pledged himself at once.

sentences.zh: 簡之聞之，殺耕牛，會聚徒眾，率以赴高祖。

translations.literal: When Jianzhi heard of it, he slaughtered a draft ox, gathered his followers, and led them to join the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi heard, slaughtered an ox for a feast, rallied his followers, and led them to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 簡之歷官至通直常侍，少府，太尉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Jianzhi rose through offices to Palace Attendant Direct in Communication, Minister of the Privy Purse, and Adviser in the Grand Commandant's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi rose to Palace Attendant Direct in Communication, Minister of the Privy Purse, and adviser on the Grand Commandant's staff.

sentences.zh: 簡之弟謙之，好學，撰《晉紀》二十卷；

translations.literal: Jianzhi's younger brother Qianzhi loved learning and compiled twenty juan of Annals of Jin;
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi's younger brother Qianzhi was a scholar who compiled twenty juan of Annals of Jin;

sentences.zh: 義熙末，為始興相。

translations.literal: at the end of the Yixi era he was Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: and at the end of the Yixi era became administrator of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 東海人徐道期流寓廣州，無士行，為僑舊所陵侮。

translations.literal: Xu Daoqi of Donghai, living in exile at Guangzhou, lacked the conduct of a gentleman and was bullied by the established émigré families.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daoqi of Donghai, an exile in Guangzhou, lacked gentlemanly conduct and was bullied by the established migrant clans.

sentences.zh: 因刺史謝欣死，合率群不逞之徒作亂，攻沒州城，殺士庶素憾者百餘，傾府庫、招集亡命，出攻始興。

translations.literal: When the Inspector Xie Xin died, he joined with a host of unruly men to rebel, stormed and took the provincial city, killed more than a hundred gentry and commoners he had long resented, emptied the treasury, gathered fugitives, and marched out to attack Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: When Inspector Xie Xin died, he rallied malcontents, seized the provincial capital, killed more than a hundred people he had long hated, emptied the treasury, recruited fugitives, and marched on Shixing.

sentences.zh: 謙之破走之，進平廣州，誅其黨與，仍行州事。

translations.literal: Qianzhi defeated and routed him, advanced to pacify Guangzhou, executed his partisans, and continued to administer the province.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi routed him, pacified Guangzhou, executed his followers, and continued to govern the province.

sentences.zh: 即以為振威將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then made General Who Shakes Might and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed General Who Shakes Might and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 後為太中大夫。

translations.literal: Later he became Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 虔之誕節，不營產業，輕財好施。

translations.literal: Qianzhi was lofty in bearing, did not build up estates, and was light with wealth and fond of giving.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi was high-spirited, cared nothing for property, and gave his money away freely.

sentences.zh: 高祖西征司馬休之、魯宗之等，遣參軍檀道濟、朱超石步騎出襄陽，虔之時為江夏相，率府郡兵力出溳城，屯三連，立橋聚糧以待。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned west against Sima Xiuzhi, Lu Zongzhi, and others, he sent the aides Tan Daoji and Zhu Chao-shi with infantry and cavalry out from Xiangyang; Qianzhi was then Administrator of Jiangxia and led the commandery and prefectural forces out from Yucheng, encamped at Sanlian, built a bridge, and gathered grain to await them.
translations.idiomatic: On the western campaign against Sima Xiuzhi and Lu Zongzhi, the emperor sent Tan Daoji and Zhu Chao-shi with infantry and cavalry from Xiangyang. Qianzhi, then administrator of Jiangxia, marched from Yucheng, encamped at Sanlian, bridged the river, and stockpiled grain for the relief force.

sentences.zh: 道濟等積日不至，為宗之子軌所襲，眾寡不敵。

translations.literal: Daoji and the others did not arrive for many days; Qianzhi was attacked by Zongzhi's son Gui; his force was too few to match the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji's column was long delayed, and Lu Zongzhi's son Gui attacked him before help arrived; he was hopelessly outnumbered.

sentences.zh: 參軍孫長庸流涕勸還軍，虔之厲色曰：「我仗順伐辠，理無不克。

translations.literal: The aide Sun Changyong wept and urged him to withdraw the army; Qianzhi said sternly: "I rely on righteousness to punish crime — by principle I cannot fail to conquer.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Sun Changyong wept and begged him to retreat. Qianzhi said sharply, "I fight in the name of justice — how can I fail?

sentences.zh: 如其不幸，命也。」

translations.literal: If it goes ill, that is fate."
translations.idiomatic: If fortune turns against me, that is fate."

sentences.zh: 戰敗見殺，追贈梁、秦二州刺史，封新康縣男，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He was defeated in battle and killed; posthumously he was given the titles of Inspector of Liang and Qin provinces, enfeoffed as Baron of Xinkang county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was defeated and killed. Posthumously he was made inspector of Liang and Qin, enfeoffed as Baron of Xinkang with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 康祖，虔之子也，襲封，為長沙王義欣鎮軍參軍，轉員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Kangzu was Qianzhi's son; he inherited the enfeoffment and served as an aide on the Pacification Army staff of the Prince of Changsha, Yixin, then was transferred to Extraordinary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzu, Qianzhi's son, inherited the title, served on Prince Yixin of Changsha's pacification army staff, and became Extraordinary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 便弓馬，膂力絕人，在閭里不治士業，以浮蕩蒱酒為事。

translations.literal: He was skilled with bow and horse and his physical strength was unmatched; in the village lanes he did not pursue the scholar's calling but made his business of roaming, dice, and wine.
translations.idiomatic: He was expert with bow and horse and possessed extraordinary strength, but in his neighborhood he neglected learning for gambling, wine, and dissolute wandering.

sentences.zh: 每犯法，為郡縣所錄，輒越屋踰牆，莫之能禽。

translations.literal: Whenever he broke the law and was recorded by the commandery and county, he would leap over roofs and scale walls, and none could seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the local authorities came for him, he leaped over roofs and walls and none could catch him.

sentences.zh: 夜入人家，為有司所圍守，康祖突圍而去，竝莫敢追。

translations.literal: He entered people's houses at night; when the authorities surrounded and held him, Kangzu broke through and fled, and none dared pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Once, after breaking into a house at night, he was surrounded by officials; he burst through the cordon and no one dared follow.

sentences.zh: 因夜還京口，半夕便至。

translations.literal: He returned that night to Jingkou and arrived within half the night.
translations.idiomatic: He fled by night to Jingkou and arrived before midnight.

sentences.zh: 明旦，守門詣府州要職。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day he was at the gatekeeper's post at the commandery and prefectural offices.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he was at his post as gatekeeper at the local government offices.

sentences.zh: 俄而建康移書錄之，府州執事者竝證康祖其夕在京口，遂見無恙。

translations.literal: Soon Jiankang sent documents to apprehend him; the officials of the commandery and prefecture all testified that Kangzu had been at Jingkou that night, and he thus escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiankang sent orders for his arrest, but the local officials all swore he had been in Jingkou that night, and he went free.

sentences.zh: 前後屢被糾劾，太祖以勳臣子，每原貸之。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly impeached before and after; Emperor Taizu, because he was the son of a meritorious minister, each time pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached again and again, Emperor Taizu pardoned him each time as the son of a meritorious servant.

sentences.zh: 為員外郎十年，再坐摴蒱戲免。

translations.literal: He served as an extraordinary attendant for ten years and twice was dismissed for dice gambling.
translations.idiomatic: He spent ten years as an extraordinary attendant and twice lost his post for gambling.

sentences.zh: 轉太子左積弩將軍，隨射聲校尉裴方明西征仇池，與方明同下廷尉，康祖免官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Strong Crossbow General of the Heir Apparent; he followed the Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot by Sound Pei Fangming on the western campaign against Chouchi; he and Fangming were both sent down to the Minister of Justice, and Kangzu was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He became Left Strong Crossbow General of the Heir Apparent and joined Pei Fangming's western campaign against Chouchi. When Fangming was sent to the Minister of Justice, Kangzu was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 頃之，世祖為豫州刺史，鎮歷陽，以康祖為征虜中兵參軍，既被委任，折節自脩。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Shizong was Inspector of Yuzhou and garrisoned Liyang; he made Kangzu a middle army aide in the Pacification Campaign headquarters; once entrusted with responsibility, he restrained himself and cultivated his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when Emperor Shizong was inspector of Yuzhou at Liyang, he appointed Kangzu a middle army aide on his staff. Once entrusted with real duties, Kangzu disciplined himself.

sentences.zh: 轉太子翊軍校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Commander of the Heir Apparent's Supporting Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made assistant commander of the heir apparent's supporting army.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷南平王鑠安蠻府司馬。

translations.literal: After a long time he was moved to Chief Administrator of the Pacify the Barbarians headquarters of the Prince of Nanping, Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he became chief administrator on Prince Shuo of Nanping's Pacify the Barbarians staff.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年春，索虜托拔燾親率大眾攻圍汝南，太祖遣諸軍救援，康祖緫統為前驅。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, the northern barbarian Tuoba Tao personally led a great host to attack and besiege Runan; Emperor Taizu sent the various armies to rescue it, and Kangzu commanded overall as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Yuanjia 27 the Rouran ruler Tuoba Tao led a great army against Runan. Emperor Taizu sent relief forces, with Kangzu in overall command of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 軍次新蔡，與虜戰，俱前百餘里，濟融水。

translations.literal: The army halted at Xincai, fought the barbarians, both sides advanced more than a hundred li, and crossed the Rong River.
translations.idiomatic: The army encamped at Xincai, engaged the enemy, and both sides pushed forward more than a hundred li before crossing the Rong River.

sentences.zh: 虜眾大至，奮擊破之，斬偽殿中尚書任城公乞地真，去縣瓠四十里，燾燒營退走。

translations.literal: The barbarian host came in great force; he fought fiercely and broke them, beheading the false Palace Attendant Within the Hall, Duke of Rencheng, Qidizhen; forty li from the county of Hu, Tao burned his camp and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy host arrived in force, he attacked with fury, broke them, and beheaded the Rouran minister Qidizhen. Forty li from Hu county, Tuoba Tao burned his camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 轉左軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲大舉北伐，康祖以歲月已晚，請待明年。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu wished to launch a great northern campaign; Kangzu, because the season was already late, asked to wait until the next year.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu planned a major northern campaign, Kangzu urged delay until the next year because the season was already late.

sentences.zh: 上以河北義徒並起，若頓兵一周，沮向義之志，不許。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that righteous partisans were rising everywhere north of the Yellow River; if the army halted for a week, it would dampen their zeal for the cause, and he did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, fearing that a week's delay would cool the ardor of the loyalist partisans rising across Hebei.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，蕭斌、王玄謨、沈慶之等入河，康祖率豫州軍出許、洛。

translations.literal: That autumn Xiao Bin, Wang Xuemo, Shen Qingzhi, and others entered the Yellow River region; Kangzu led the Yuzhou army out toward Xu and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Xiao Bin, Wang Xuemo, and Shen Qingzhi crossed the Yellow River while Kangzu led the Yuzhou army toward Xu and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 玄謨等敗歸，虜引大眾南度。

translations.literal: Xuemo and the others were defeated and returned; the barbarians led a great host south across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo's force was beaten back, and the barbarians drove a great army south across the river.

sentences.zh: 南平王鑠在壽陽，上慮為所圍，召康祖速反。

translations.literal: The Prince of Nanping, Shuo, was at Shouyang; the emperor feared he would be surrounded and summoned Kangzu to return quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shuo of Nanping was at Shouyang; fearing he would be encircled, the emperor ordered Kangzu to hurry back.

sentences.zh: 康祖回軍，未至壽陽數十里，會虜永昌王庫仁真以長安之眾八萬騎，與康祖相及於尉武。

translations.literal: Kangzu turned his army back; when he was still several tens of li from Shouyang, it happened that the barbarian Prince of Yongchang, Kurenzhen, with eighty thousand horsemen from the forces of Chang'an, caught up with Kangzu at Yuwu.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzu was still several tens of li from Shouyang when the Rouran Prince of Yongchang, Kurenzhen, overtook him at Yuwu with eighty thousand cavalry from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 康祖凡有八千人，軍副胡盛之欲附山依險，間行取至。

translations.literal: Kangzu had in all eight thousand men; his deputy Hu Shengzhi wished to cling to the mountains and rely on difficult terrain, going by hidden paths to reach Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzu had only eight thousand men. His deputy Hu Shengzhi wanted to slip through the hills by a hidden route to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 康祖怒曰：「吾受命本朝，清蕩河洛。

translations.literal: Kangzu said angrily: "I have received orders from our dynasty to clear and pacify the He and Luo region.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzu snapped, "I was sent by the dynasty to clear the He and Luo country.

sentences.zh: 寇今自送，不復遠勞王師，犬羊雖多，實易摧滅。

translations.literal: The enemy now delivers himself — we need not trouble the imperial army from afar; though the dogs and sheep are many, they are in truth easy to crush and destroy.
translations.idiomatic: The foe has delivered himself — no need to trouble the imperial army from afar. However many these sheep and dogs may be, they are easily destroyed.

sentences.zh: 吾兵精器練，去壽陽裁數十里，援軍尋至，亦何患乎！」

translations.literal: Our troops are elite and our weapons well trained; we are only several tens of li from Shouyang, and relief will soon arrive — what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: Our men are seasoned and our arms sharp; Shouyang is only a few tens of li away, and relief will come soon. What is there to fear!"

sentences.zh: 乃結車營而進。

translations.literal: He then formed a wagon encampment and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He formed a wagon laager and marched forward.

sentences.zh: 虜四面來攻，大戰一日一夜，殺虜填積。

translations.literal: The barbarians attacked from all four sides; they fought a great battle for a day and a night, and the slain barbarians piled up.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy attacked from every side. For a day and a night they fought until the dead barbarians lay in heaps.

sentences.zh: 虜分眾為三，且休且戰，以騎負草燒車營。

translations.literal: The barbarians divided their forces into three groups, resting and fighting in turn, and used horsemen carrying grass to burn the wagon camp.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy split into three bands, fighting and resting in relays, and sent horsemen with bundles of grass to set the laager ablaze.

sentences.zh: 康祖率厲將士，無不一當百，虜死者太半。

translations.literal: Kangzu led and roused his officers and men; each fought as one against a hundred, and more than half the barbarians died.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzu drove his men until each fought like a hundred; more than half the enemy perished.

sentences.zh: 會矢中頸死，於是大敗，舉營淪覆，為虜所殺盡，自免者裁數十人。

translations.literal: It happened that an arrow struck his neck and he died; then came the great defeat; the whole camp was overrun; all were killed by the barbarians, and only several tens escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Then an arrow struck his neck and killed him. The army collapsed; the camp was overrun and nearly all were slaughtered. Only a few dozen escaped.

sentences.zh: 虜傳康祖首示彭城，面如生。

translations.literal: The barbarians paraded Kangzu's head before Pengcheng; his face was as in life.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy displayed Kangzu's head before Pengcheng; his face still looked alive.

sentences.zh: 胡盛之為虜生禽，托跋燾寵之，常在左右。

translations.literal: Hu Shengzhi was captured alive by the barbarians; Tuoba Tao favored him and kept him always at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shengzhi was taken alive. Tuoba Tao favored him and kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 盛之有勇力，初為長沙王義欣鎮軍參軍督護，討劫譙郡，縣西劫有馬步七十，逃隱深榛，盛之挺身獨進，手斬五十八級。

translations.literal: Shengzhi had courage and strength; he was first an army aide and commander of guards on the Pacification Army staff of the Prince of Changsha, Yixin; in suppressing bandits in Qiao commandery, seventy bandits with horse and foot on the west of the county fled into deep thickets; Shengzhi advanced alone with bared body and personally beheaded fifty-eight of them.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzhi was famed for strength. As an aide on Prince Yixin of Changsha's staff, he hunted bandits in Qiao. Seventy raiders fled into deep brush; he went in alone and killed fifty-eight with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，詔曰：「康祖班師尉武，戎律靡忒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year an edict said: "Kangzu withdrew his army at Yuwu; in military discipline he was without error.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-eight an edict declared, "At Yuwu Kangzu withdrew his army without breach of military law.

sentences.zh: 對眾以寡，殲殄太半。

translations.literal: Facing a multitude with few men, he annihilated more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Though outnumbered, he destroyed more than half the foe.

sentences.zh: 猛氣雲騰，志申力屈，沒世徇節，良可嘉悼。

translations.literal: His fierce spirit rose like clouds; his will was fulfilled but his strength failed; he died upholding his duty — truly worthy of praise and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: His fury rose like storm clouds; his will was fulfilled though his strength failed; he died loyal to his post — a death worthy of honor and grief.

sentences.zh: 宜加甄寵，以旌忠烈。

translations.literal: He should receive added honors to mark his loyal valor.
translations.idiomatic: Let honors be added to proclaim his loyal courage.

sentences.zh: 可贈益州刺史，諡曰壯男。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Inspector of Yizhou, with the posthumous title Strong Baron."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously made inspector of Yizhou with the posthumous title Strong Baron."

sentences.zh: 傳國至齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: The fief passed down until Qi received the abdication, when the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed down until Qi took the throne, when the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 垣護之，字彥宗，略陽桓道人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Huzhi, courtesy name Yanzong, was a man of Huandao in Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huzhi, styled Yanzong, came from Huandao in Lueyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖敞，仕苻氏，為長樂國郎中令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chang served the Fu clan and was Director of Gentlemen of the Principality of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chang had served the Former Qin and become director of gentlemen for the Principality of Changle.

sentences.zh: 慕容德入青州，以敞為車騎長史。

translations.literal: When Murong De entered Qingzhou, he made Chang Chief Clerk of the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong De took Qingzhou, he made Chang chief clerk on his chariots and cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 德兄子超襲偽位，伯父遵、父苗復見委任。

translations.literal: When De's brother's son Chao seized the false throne, his father's elder brother Zun and his father Miao were again entrusted with office.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chao seized the throne, Huzhi's uncle Zun and father Miao were again given high posts.

sentences.zh: 遵為尚書，苗京兆太守。

translations.literal: Zun became Minister of the Masters of Writing; Miao was Prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zun became a minister of writing; Miao became prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 高祖圍廣固，遵、苗踰城歸降，竝以為太尉行參軍。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor besieged Guanggu, Zun and Miao crossed the wall to surrender and were both made acting aides on the Grand Commandant's staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor besieged Guanggu, Zun and Miao climbed the wall to surrender and both became acting aides on the Grand Commandant's staff.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉中，遵為員外散騎常侍，苗屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era under Emperor Taizu, Zun was an Extraordinary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Miao was Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizu in the Yuanjia era, Zun was an extraordinary attendant of the scattered cavalry and Miao was colonel of the garrison cavalry.

sentences.zh: 護之少倜儻，不拘小節，形狀短陋，而氣榦彊果。

translations.literal: Huzhi in youth was bold and free, not bound by small proprieties; his form was short and plain, but his spirit was strong and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhi was bold and careless of convention in youth; though short and plain in appearance, his spirit was fierce and resolute.

sentences.zh: 從高祖征司馬休之，為世子中軍府長史，兼行參軍。

translations.literal: He followed the Founding Emperor in the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi and served as Chief Clerk of the Heir Apparent's Central Army headquarters, concurrently as an acting aide.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi as chief clerk on the heir apparent's central army staff and acting aide.

sentences.zh: 永初中，補奉朝請。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongchu era he was appointed Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongchu era he became an attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，為殿中將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia he was a Palace General.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanjia he was made a palace general.

sentences.zh: 隨到彥之北伐，彥之將回師，護之為書諫曰：「外聞節下欲回師反斾，竊所不同。

translations.literal: He followed Dao Yanzhi on the northern campaign; when Yanzhi was about to turn the army back, Huzhi wrote a remonstrance saying: "From outside I hear that Your Lordship wishes to turn the army and reverse the banners — I privately disagree.
translations.idiomatic: On Dao Yanzhi's northern campaign, when Yanzhi prepared to withdraw, Huzhi wrote in protest, "I hear that you mean to turn the army homeward — I cannot agree.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 殘虜畏威，望風奔迸，八載侵地，不戰克復。

translations.literal: The broken barbarians fear our might and flee at sight of our banners; lands they held for eight years have been recovered without battle.
translations.idiomatic: The broken enemy fears our might and flees at our banners; territory they held for eight years has been recovered almost without a fight.

sentences.zh: 方當長驅朔漠，窮掃遺醜，況乃自送，無假遠勞。

translations.literal: We should now drive far into the northern deserts and utterly sweep away the remnant villains — all the more since they deliver themselves and we need not trouble ourselves from afar.
translations.idiomatic: We should drive deep into the northern wastes and wipe out the remnant foe — especially now that they are delivering themselves without need of a long campaign.

sentences.zh: 宜使竺靈秀速進滑臺助朱脩之固守，節下大軍進擬河北，則牢、洛游魂，自然奔退。

translations.literal: Zhu Lingxiu should be sent to advance quickly to Huatai to help Zhu Xiuzhi hold firm; Your Lordship's great army should advance toward Hebei, and then the wandering souls of Lao and Luoyang will naturally flee and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Send Zhu Lingxiu quickly to Huatai to reinforce Zhu Xiuzhi, while your main force presses toward Hebei; the garrisons at Hulao and Luoyang will then collapse of themselves.

sentences.zh: 且昔人有連年攻戰，失眾乏糧者，猶張膽爭前，莫肯輕退。

translations.literal: Moreover, men of old who fought year after year, losing troops and running short of grain, still dared to press forward and would not lightly withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Men of old fought for years even after losing troops and grain, yet still pressed forward and would not lightly retreat.

sentences.zh: 況今青州豐穰，濟漕流通，士馬飽逸，威力無損。

translations.literal: How much more now, when Qingzhou is rich in harvest, transport on the Ji canal flows freely, men and horses are full and rested, and our fighting strength is unimpaired.
translations.idiomatic: How much more now, when Qingzhou is abundant, the Ji canal open, men and horses rested, and our strength unbroken.

sentences.zh: 若空棄滑臺，坐喪成業，豈是朝廷受任之旨。」

translations.literal: If we abandon Huatai for nothing and sit by while our achievement is lost, how can that be the intent of the court's commission?"
translations.idiomatic: To abandon Huatai and throw away what we have won — is that the charge the court gave you?"

sentences.zh: 彥之不納，散敗而歸。

translations.literal: Yanzhi did not accept it and returned in scattered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi ignored him and returned in rout.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞而善之，以補江夏王義恭征北行參軍、北高平太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu heard of it and approved, appointing him acting aide on the Northern Campaign staff of the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, and Prefect of Northern Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu approved and made him acting aide on Prince Yigong of Jiangxia's northern campaign staff and prefect of northern Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 以載禁物繫尚方，久之蒙宥。

translations.literal: For carrying forbidden goods he was imprisoned in the Imperial Workshops; after a long time he received pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned in the imperial workshops for carrying contraband, but was pardoned after a long interval.

sentences.zh: 又補衡陽王義季征北長流參軍，遷宣威將軍、鍾離太守。

translations.literal: He was again appointed senior flowing aide on the Northern Campaign staff of the Prince of Hengyang, Yiji, then promoted to General Who Proclaims Might and Prefect of Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: He then served on Prince Yiji of Hengyang's northern staff, became General Who Proclaims Might, and was made prefect of Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 隨王玄謨入河，玄謨攻滑臺，護之百舸為前鋒，進據石濟；

translations.literal: He followed Wang Xuemo in entering the Yellow River region; Xuemo attacked Huatai; Huzhi with a hundred boats served as vanguard and advanced to occupy Shiji;
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wang Xuemo across the Yellow River. When Xuemo besieged Huatai, Huzhi led a hundred boats as vanguard and seized Shiji;

sentences.zh: 石濟在滑臺西南百二十里。

translations.literal: Shiji was one hundred and twenty li southwest of Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji lay a hundred and twenty li southwest of Huatai.

sentences.zh: 及虜救至，又馳書勸玄謨急攻，曰：「昔武皇攻廣固，死沒者亦眾。

translations.literal: When barbarian relief arrived, he again sent a urgent letter urging Xuemo to attack quickly, saying: "In former days the Martial Emperor attacked Guanggu, and those who died were also many.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy relief arrived, he urged Xuemo by urgent letter to press the assault: "When the Martial Emperor took Guanggu, many men died as well.

sentences.zh: 況事殊曩日，豈得計士眾傷疲，願以屠城為急。」

translations.literal: How much more when the situation differs from those days — how can we reckon the weariness and wounds of officers and men? I beg that storming the city be made the urgent task."
translations.idiomatic: Today's situation is far better — you cannot weigh casualties against victory. Take the city at once."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: Xuemo did not follow the advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo refused.

sentences.zh: 玄謨敗退，不暇報護之。

translations.literal: Xuemo was defeated and withdrew, with no time to inform Huzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo was beaten and fled without warning Huzhi.

sentences.zh: 護之聞知，而虜悉已牽玄謨水軍大艚，連以鐵鏁三重斷河，欲以絕護之還路。

translations.literal: When Huzhi heard, the barbarians had already towed away Xuemo's great naval vessels and chained the river with iron cables in three layers to cut off Huzhi's route of return.
translations.idiomatic: When Huzhi learned of it, the enemy had already seized Xuemo's great ships and stretched three lines of iron chains across the river to block his retreat.

sentences.zh: 河水迅急，護之中流而下，每至鐵鏁，以長柯斧斷之，虜不能禁。

translations.literal: The river water ran swift; Huzhi went downstream through mid-current; whenever he reached an iron chain he used a long-handled axe to cut it, and the barbarians could not stop him.
translations.idiomatic: The current was fierce. Huzhi ran downstream and, at each chain, chopped it apart with a long-handled axe; the enemy could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 唯失一舸，餘舸竝全。

translations.literal: He lost only one boat; the rest were all preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He lost only one boat; the rest escaped intact.

sentences.zh: 留戍靡溝城。

translations.literal: He left a garrison at Migou city.
translations.idiomatic: He left a garrison at Migou.

sentences.zh: 還為江夏王義恭驃騎戶曹參軍，戍淮陰。

translations.literal: On his return he became an aide in the Household Accounts section of the Rapid Cavalry staff of the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, and garrisoned Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to serve on Prince Yigong of Jiangxia's staff and garrisoned Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 加建武將軍，領濟北太守。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title General Who Establishes Martiality and acted as Prefect of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Establishes Martiality and acting prefect of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 率二千人復隨張永攻碻磝，先據委粟津。

translations.literal: Leading two thousand men he again followed Zhang Yong in attacking Que'ao and first seized Weisu Ford.
translations.idiomatic: With two thousand men he again joined Zhang Yong against Que'ao and seized Weisu Ford first.

sentences.zh: 虜杜道俊與偽尚書伏連來援碻磝，護之拒之，賊因引軍東去。

translations.literal: The barbarian Du Daojun and the false Minister Fulian came to relieve Que'ao; Huzhi repelled them, and the rebels therefore led their army east.
translations.idiomatic: Du Daojun and the Rouran minister Fulian came to relieve Que'ao; Huzhi drove them off and the enemy marched east.

sentences.zh: 蕭思話遣護之迎軍至梁山，偽尚書韓元興率精騎卒至，護之依險拒戰，斬其都軍長史，甲首數十，賊乃退。

translations.literal: Xiao Sihua sent Huzhi to meet the army at Liangshan; the false Minister Han Yuanxing led elite cavalry that arrived in a rush; Huzhi relied on difficult terrain to resist, beheaded their army commander's chief clerk, took several tens of heads in armor, and the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sihua sent Huzhi to meet the army at Liangshan. Han Yuanxing arrived with elite cavalry; Huzhi fought from rough ground, killed their army commander's chief clerk, took dozens of heads, and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 思話將引還，誑護之云：「沈慶之救軍垂至，可急於濟口立橋。」

translations.literal: Sihua was about to withdraw and deceived Huzhi, saying: "Shen Qingzhi's relief force is almost here — you should quickly build a bridge at the Ji ford."
translations.idiomatic: Sihua planned to withdraw and tricked Huzhi, saying, "Shen Qingzhi's relief is nearly here — build a bridge quickly at the Ji crossing."

sentences.zh: 護之揣知其意，即分遣白丁。

translations.literal: Huzhi guessed his intent and at once sent out laborers in detachments.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhi saw through the ruse and sent out labor parties at once.

sentences.zh: 思話復令度河戍乞活堡，以防追軍。

translations.literal: Sihua again ordered him to cross the river and garrison Qihuo Fort against pursuing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua then ordered him across the river to hold Qihuo Fort against pursuit.

sentences.zh: 三十年春，太祖崩，遷屯歷下。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirtieth year Emperor Taizu died; Huzhi moved his camp to Lixia.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year thirty Emperor Taizu died, and Huzhi moved his camp to Lixia.

sentences.zh: 聞世祖入討，率所領馳赴，上嘉之，以為督冀州、青州之濟南、樂安、太原三郡諸軍事、寧遠將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Hearing that Emperor Shizong had entered on a punitive campaign, he led his command in a rapid rush to join; the emperor praised him and made him Commander over the military affairs of Ji, Qing, and the three commanderies Jinan, Le'an, and Taiyuan, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and Inspector of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong marched to suppress the rebels, Huzhi raced to join him. The emperor praised his loyalty and made him commander over Ji and Qing, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，南郡王義宣反，兗州刺史徐遺寶，護之妻弟也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian the Prince of Nanjun, Yixuan, rebelled; Xu Yibao, Inspector of Yanzhou, was Huzhi's wife's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 1 Prince Yixuan of Nanjun rebelled. Xu Yibao, inspector of Yanzhou, was Huzhi's brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 遠相連結，與護之書，勸使同逆。

translations.literal: From afar they were in contact; he wrote to Huzhi urging him to join the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: They were in contact from afar, and Yibao wrote urging Huzhi to rebel with them.

sentences.zh: 護之馳使以聞。

translations.literal: Huzhi sent a fast messenger to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhi sent an urgent report to court.

sentences.zh: 遺寶時戍湖陸，護之留子恭祖守歷城，自率步騎襲遺寶。

translations.literal: Yibao was then garrisoning Hulu; Huzhi left his son Gongzu to hold Licheng and personally led infantry and cavalry in a surprise attack on Yibao.
translations.idiomatic: Yibao was at Hulu. Huzhi left his son Gongzu at Licheng and led infantry and cavalry against him.

sentences.zh: 道經鄒山，破其別戍。

translations.literal: Passing Zou Mountain, he broke their detached garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Marching past Zou Mountain, he destroyed a detached garrison.

sentences.zh: 未至湖陸六十里，遺寶焚城西走。

translations.literal: When he was still sixty li from Hulu, Yibao burned the city and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty li from Hulu, Yibao burned the city and fled west.

sentences.zh: 兗土既定，徵為游擊將軍。

translations.literal: When Yan territory was settled, he was summoned as General of Mobile Strikes.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yan was pacified, he was recalled as General of Mobile Strikes.

sentences.zh: 隨沈慶之等擊魯爽，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He followed Shen Qingzhi and others in attacking Lu Shuang and was given the additional title General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Shen Qingzhi against Lu Shuang and was made General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 義宣率大眾至梁山，與王玄謨相持。

translations.literal: Yixuan led a great host to Liangshan and faced Wang Xuemo in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan brought a great army to Liangshan and locked in stalemate with Wang Xuemo.

sentences.zh: 柳元景率護之及護之弟詢之、柳叔仁、鄭琨等諸軍，出鎮新亭。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanjing led Huzhi, Huzhi's younger brother Xunzhi, Liu Shuren, Zheng Kun, and the various armies out to garrison Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing led Huzhi, his brother Xunzhi, Liu Shuren, Zheng Kun, and other forces to garrison Xinting.

sentences.zh: 玄謨見賊強盛，遣司馬管法濟求救甚急。

translations.literal: Xuemo, seeing the rebels strong, sent his Major Guan Faji with an extremely urgent plea for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the rebels' strength, Xuemo sent his major Guan Faji with an urgent plea for help.

sentences.zh: 上遣元景等進據南州，護之水軍先發。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Yuanjing and others to advance and hold the southern region; Huzhi's naval force set out first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yuanjing south; Huzhi's fleet sailed first.

sentences.zh: 賊遣將龐法起率眾襲姑孰，適值護之、鄭琨等至，奮擊，大破之，斬獲及投水死略盡。

translations.literal: The rebels sent the general Pang Faqi leading troops to strike Gudu; it happened that Huzhi, Zheng Kun, and others arrived; they fought fiercely and inflicted a great defeat; those beheaded, captured, and drowned were nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent Pang Faqi against Gudu just as Huzhi and Zheng Kun arrived. They attacked fiercely and nearly annihilated the enemy by blade and drowning.

sentences.zh: 玄謨馳信告元景曰：「西城不守，唯餘東城，眾寡相懸，請退還姑孰，更議進取。」

translations.literal: Xuemo sent a fast letter telling Yuanjing: "The western city cannot be held; only the eastern city remains; our numbers are far fewer than theirs; I ask to withdraw to Gudu and discuss advance again."
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo wrote urgently to Yuanjing, "The west bank is lost and only the east holds. We are badly outnumbered. Withdraw to Gudu and plan again."

sentences.zh: 元景不許，將悉眾赴救，護之勸分軍援之。

translations.literal: Yuanjing did not agree and was about to lead all his forces to the rescue; Huzhi urged dividing the army to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing refused and prepared to march in full force; Huzhi urged sending only part of the army.

sentences.zh: 元景然其計，乃以精兵配護之赴梁山。

translations.literal: Yuanjing approved his plan and then assigned elite troops to Huzhi to go to Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing agreed and gave Huzhi picked troops for Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 及戰，護之見賊舟艦累遝，謂玄謨曰：「今當以火平之。」

translations.literal: When battle came, Huzhi saw the rebel ships piled layer on layer and said to Xuemo: "We should now use fire to settle them."
translations.idiomatic: In the battle Huzhi saw the enemy ships massed thick and told Xuemo, "We must settle this with fire."

sentences.zh: 即使隊主張談等燒賊艦，風猛水急，賊軍以此奔散。

translations.literal: He at once had the squad leader Zhang Tan and others burn the rebel ships; wind was fierce and water swift, and the rebel army scattered in flight for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zhang Tan and others set the enemy fleet ablaze. Wind and current did the rest, and the rebel fleet scattered.

sentences.zh: 梁山平，護之率軍追討，會朱脩之以平江陵，至尋陽而還。

translations.literal: When Liangshan was pacified, Huzhi led his army in pursuit; it happened that Zhu Xiuzhi had pacified Jiangling; he reached Xunyang and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Liangshan fell, Huzhi pursued the enemy until Zhu Xiuzhi pacified Jiangling; he went as far as Xunyang and returned.

sentences.zh: 遷督徐、兗二州、豫州之梁郡諸軍事、寧朔將軍、徐州刺史，封益陽縣侯。

translations.literal: He was moved to Commander over the military affairs of Xu and Yan provinces and Liang commandery of Yuzhou, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Xuzhou, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yiyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander over Xu and Yan, General Who Pacifies the North, inspector of Xuzhou, and Marquis of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 食邑千戶。

translations.literal: His fief was one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 弟詢之，驍敢有氣力，元兇夙聞其名，以副輔國將軍張柬。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xunzhi was fierce and bold with great physical strength; the arch-criminal had long heard his name and made him deputy to the General Who Assists the State, Zhang Dong.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xunzhi was fierce and powerful. The usurper had long heard of him and made him deputy to Zhang Dong, General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 時張超首行大逆，亦領軍隸柬。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Chao was the first to commit the great treason and also commanded troops subordinate to Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao, who had led the great treason, also commanded troops under Dong.

sentences.zh: 詢之規殺之，慮柬不同，柬宿有此志，又未測詢之同否，互相觀察。

translations.literal: Xunzhi plotted to kill him but feared Dong would not agree; Dong had long harbored this intent yet could not tell whether Xunzhi agreed; they watched one another.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhi planned to kill Chao but feared Dong would not agree. Dong had long wanted the same yet could not tell if Xunzhi would join him; each watched the other.

sentences.zh: 會超來論事，柬色動，詢之覺之，即共定謀，遣信召超。

translations.literal: When Chao came to discuss affairs, Dong's expression changed; Xunzhi noticed it, and they at once fixed their plot together and sent a message summoning Chao.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao came to discuss business, Dong's face changed. Xunzhi noticed, they sealed their plot, and sent for Chao.

sentences.zh: 超疑之，不至，改宿他所。

translations.literal: Chao suspected them, did not come, and changed to lodge elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Chao grew suspicious, stayed away, and lodged elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 詢之不知其移，逕斫之，殺其僕於牀，因與柬南奔。

translations.literal: Xunzhi did not know he had moved and went straight to hack at him, killing his servant on the bed; he then fled south with Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing Chao had moved, Xunzhi struck at the bed and killed a servant; he and Dong fled south.

sentences.zh: 柬溺淮死，詢之得至。

translations.literal: Dong drowned in the Huai and died; Xunzhi reached safety.
translations.idiomatic: Dong drowned in the Huai; Xunzhi escaped.

sentences.zh: 時世祖已即位，以為積弩將軍。

translations.literal: By then Emperor Shizong had already taken the throne and made him Strong Crossbow General.
translations.idiomatic: By then Emperor Shizong had ascended the throne and made him Strong Crossbow General.

sentences.zh: 梁山之役力戰，為流矢所中。

translations.literal: At the battle of Liangshan he fought fiercely and was struck by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: He fought fiercely at Liangshan and was struck by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 死，追贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 二年，護之坐論功挾私，免官。

translations.literal: In the second year Huzhi, because in discussing merit he mixed in private favor, was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he was dismissed for letting private favor sway his judgment of merit.

sentences.zh: 復為游擊將軍。

translations.literal: He was again made General of Mobile Strikes.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as General of Mobile Strikes.

sentences.zh: 俄遷大司馬，輔國將軍，領南東海太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Grand Marshal, General Who Assists the State, and acting Prefect of Southern Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Grand Marshal and General Who Assists the State, and acting prefect of southern Donghai.

sentences.zh: 未拜，復督青、冀二州諸軍事、寧遠將軍、青、冀二州刺史，鎮歷城。

translations.literal: Before he took the appointment, he was again made Commander over the military affairs of Qing and Ji provinces, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and Inspector of Qing and Ji, garrisoning Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Before he assumed the post he was made commander over Qing and Ji, General Who Pacifies the Distance, inspector of both provinces, and garrison commander at Licheng.

sentences.zh: 明年，進號寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: The next year his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 進督徐州之東莞、東安二郡軍事。

translations.literal: He was further made Commander over the military affairs of the two commanderies Dongguan and Dong'an in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given command over Dongguan and Dong'an in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 世祖以歷下要害，欲移青州并鎮歷城。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, because Lixia was strategically vital, wished to move Qingzhou and combine its garrison with Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lixia was strategically vital, Emperor Shizong wanted to move the Qingzhou headquarters to Licheng.

sentences.zh: 議者多異。

translations.literal: Many in the deliberations disagreed.
translations.idiomatic: Many at court disagreed.

sentences.zh: 護之曰：「青州北有河、濟，又多陂澤，非虜所向。

translations.literal: Huzhi said: "North of Qingzhou are the Yellow and Ji rivers, and there are many marshes and lakes — not where the barbarians aim.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhi argued, "North of Qingzhou lie the Yellow and Ji rivers and many marshes — not where barbarians strike.

sentences.zh: 每來寇掠，必由歷城，二州并鎮，此經遠之略也。

translations.literal: Whenever they come to raid and plunder, they must pass through Licheng; to garrison both provinces together here is the enduring long-term strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Every raid passes through Licheng. Garrisoning both provinces there is the sound long-term strategy.

sentences.zh: 北又近河，歸順者易，近息民患，遠申王威，安邊之上計也。」

translations.literal: To the north it is also close to the rivers, so those who submit are easily won; nearby the people's troubles are calmed, afar the king's majesty is displayed — the supreme plan for securing the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: It is close to the northern rivers, so defectors come easily; nearby it eases the people's burdens, afar it displays royal power — the best plan for securing the border."

sentences.zh: 由是遂定。

translations.literal: For this reason the decision was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 子承祖嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chengzu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengzu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 承祖卒，子顯宗嗣。

translations.literal: When Chengzu died, his son Xianzong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu died, his son Xianzong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 護之次子恭祖，勇果有父風。

translations.literal: Huzhi's second son Gongzu was brave and resolute with his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhi's second son Gongzu was bold and resolute in his father's mold.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始初，以軍功為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taishi era under Emperor Taizong, through military merit he became Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Taizong's Taishi era he became inspector of Liang and southern Qin for his military service.

sentences.zh: 遵子閬，元嘉中，為員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Zun's son Lang, in the Yuanjia era, was an Extraordinary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's son Lang served as extraordinary attendant of the scattered cavalry in the Yuanjia era.

sentences.zh: 母墓為東阿寺道人曇洛等所發，閬與弟殿中將軍閎共殺曇洛等五人，詣官歸罪，見原。

translations.literal: His mother's tomb was opened by the monk Tanluo of Dong'a Temple and others; Lang and his younger brother Hong, a Palace General, together killed Tanluo and four others, went to the authorities to surrender guilt, and were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When monks from Dong'a Temple robbed his mother's tomb, Lang and his brother Hong, a palace general, killed five of them, surrendered at court, and were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 閬，大明三年，自義興太守為寧朔將軍、兗州刺史，為竟陵王誕所殺。

translations.literal: Lang, in the third year of Daming, from Administrator of Yixing was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yanzhou, and was killed by the Prince of Jingling, Dan.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 3 Lang rose from administrator of Yixing to General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Yanzhou, and was killed by Prince Dan of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 追贈征虜將軍，刺史如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, with inspector's rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, retaining his inspector's rank.

sentences.zh: 閎，順帝昇明末，右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Hong, at the end of the Shengming era under Emperor Shun, was General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Hong became General of the Right Guard late in Emperor Shun's Shengming era.

sentences.zh: 張興世，字文德，竟陵竟陵人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingshi, courtesy name Wende, was a native of Jingling in Jingling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xingshi, styled Wende, came from Jingling in Jingling commandery.

sentences.zh: 本單名世，太宗益為興世。

translations.literal: He was originally surnamed with the single given name Shi; Emperor Taizong added to make Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: His original given name was Shi; Emperor Taizong expanded it to Xingshi.

sentences.zh: 少時家貧，南郡宗珍之為竟陵郡，興世依之為客。

translations.literal: In youth his family was poor; Zong Zhenzhi of Nanjun was prefect of Jingling, and Xingshi attached to him as a client.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor in youth. When Zong Zhenzhi of Nanjun became prefect of Jingling, Xingshi joined him as a retainer.

sentences.zh: 竟陵舊置軍府，以補參軍督護，不就。

translations.literal: Jingling had long maintained a military headquarters; he was offered appointment as army aide and commander of guards but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When offered a staff post at the old Jingling military headquarters, he declined.

sentences.zh: 白衣隨王玄謨伐蠻，每戰，輒有禽獲，玄謨舊部曲諸將不及也，甚奇之。

translations.literal: As a commoner in white he followed Wang Xuemo in campaigning against the Man tribes; in every battle he always had captures; Xuemo's old subordinate generals could not match him, and Xuemo marveled at him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: As a common soldier he followed Wang Xuemo against the Man tribes and took captives in every fight, outdoing Xuemo's veteran officers. Xuemo was astonished.

sentences.zh: 興世還都，白太祖，稱其膽力。

translations.literal: Xingshi returned to the capital and reported to Emperor Taizu, praising his courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, he praised Xingshi's courage to Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 後隨世祖鎮尋陽，以補南中參軍督護。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Shizong in garrisoning Xunyang and was appointed aide and commander of guards in the Southern Center headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Shizong to Xunyang as an aide and guard commander.

sentences.zh: 入討元兇，隸柳元景為前鋒。

translations.literal: He entered on the campaign to suppress the arch-criminal and served under Liu Yuanjing as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against the usurper he served under Liu Yuanjing as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 事定，轉員外將軍，領從隊。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he was transferred to Extraordinary General and commanded the escort detachment.
translations.idiomatic: After the revolt was crushed he became extraordinary general and led the escort detachment.

sentences.zh: 南郡王義宣反，又隨玄謨出梁山，有戰功。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Nanjun, Yixuan, rebelled, he again followed Xuemo to Liangshan and had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yixuan of Nanjun rebelled, he again followed Xuemo to Liangshan and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 除建平王宏中軍行參軍，領長刀。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting aide on the Central Army staff of the Prince of Jianping, Hong, and commanded the long-blade troops.
translations.idiomatic: He became acting aide on Prince Hong of Jianping's central army staff and commanded the long-blade troops.

sentences.zh: 又隸西平王子尚為直衛。

translations.literal: He again served under the Prince of Xiping, Zishang, as a direct guard.
translations.idiomatic: He then served as a direct guard to Prince Zishang of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 坐從子尚入臺，棄仗游走，下獄，免官。

translations.literal: Because he followed Zishang into the palace platform, cast aside his weapons and roamed about, he was imprisoned and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: For following Zishang into the palace, casting aside his weapons, and roaming the halls, he was jailed and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 復以白衣充直衛。

translations.literal: He again served as a direct guard in commoner's dress.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as a guard, this time in commoner's dress.

sentences.zh: 大明末，除員外散騎侍郎，仍除宣威將軍、隨郡太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Daming he was appointed Extraordinary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry and at the same time General Who Proclaims Might and Prefect of Suijun.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daming he was made extraordinary gentleman of the scattered cavalry, General Who Proclaims Might, and prefect of Suijun.

sentences.zh: 未行，太宗即位，四方反叛。

translations.literal: Before he departed, Emperor Taizong took the throne and rebellion broke out on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up his post, Emperor Taizong ascended the throne and rebellions erupted everywhere.

sentences.zh: 進興世號龍驤將軍，領水軍，距南賊於赭圻。

translations.literal: Xingshi's title was advanced to General of the Soaring Dragon; he led the naval force and blocked the southern rebels at Zheqi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Soaring Dragon, given command of the fleet, and posted against the southern rebels at Zheqi.

sentences.zh: 築二城於湖口，偽龍驤將軍陳慶領舸於前為游軍。

translations.literal: They built two cities at Hukou; the false General of the Soaring Dragon Chen Qing led boats in front as mobile troops.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels built two forts at Hukou; their General of the Soaring Dragon Chen Qing led a mobile fleet ahead.

sentences.zh: 興世率龍驤將軍佼長生、董凱之攻克二城，因擊慶，慶戰大敗，投水死者數千人。

translations.literal: Xingshi led the Generals of the Soaring Dragon Jiao Changsheng and Dong Kaizhi in storming the two cities, then struck Qing; Qing was greatly defeated in battle and several thousand drowned after casting themselves into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi, Jiao Changsheng, and Dong Kaizhi took both forts, then routed Chen Qing; thousands drowned trying to escape.

sentences.zh: 時臺軍據赭圻，南賊屯鵲尾，相持久不決。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial army held Zheqi and the southern rebels encamped at Quewei; they faced each other in stalemate for a long time without decision.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army held Zheqi while the rebels camped at Quewei, and the stalemate dragged on.

sentences.zh: 興世建議曰：「賊據上流，兵強地勝。

translations.literal: Xingshi proposed: "The rebels hold the upper stream; their troops are strong and their ground advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi proposed, "The rebels hold the upper river, with strong troops and favorable ground.

sentences.zh: 我今雖相持有餘，而制敵不足。

translations.literal: We now, though we have surplus strength for stalemate, lack enough to control the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: We can hold our own in stalemate, but we cannot master them.

sentences.zh: 今若以兵數千，潛出其上，因險自固，隨宜斷截，使其首尾周遑，進退疑沮，中流一梗，糧運自艱。

translations.literal: If we now take several thousand troops and secretly go out above them, rely on difficult terrain to secure ourselves, and cut them off as occasion demands, we can make their head and tail look about in confusion, their advance and retreat doubtful and hesitant; one blockage in midstream and their grain transport will naturally grow difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Send several thousand men secretly upstream, fortify a strong position, and cut their communications at will. Their front and rear will fall into confusion, their movements uncertain; block midstream and their grain convoys will fail.

sentences.zh: 制賊之奇，莫過於此。」

translations.literal: In strange measures for controlling the enemy, nothing surpasses this."
translations.idiomatic: No stratagem could be stranger or more effective."

sentences.zh: 沈攸之、吳喜並贊其計。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi and Wu Xi both praised his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi and Wu Xi both endorsed the plan.

sentences.zh: 時豫州刺史殷琰之據壽陽同逆，為劉勔所攻，南賊遣龐孟虯率軍助琰，劉勔遣信求援甚急。

translations.literal: At that time Yin Yan of Yuzhou held Shouyang in joint rebellion and was attacked by Liu Yu; the southern rebels sent Pang Mengjiao leading troops to aid Yan, and Liu Yu sent a message begging relief with extreme urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yan of Yuzhou held Shouyang for the rebels and was besieged by Liu Yu. The rebels sent Pang Mengjiao to relieve him, and Liu Yu begged urgently for help.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁欲遣興世救之，問沈攸之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jian'an, Xiuren, wished to send Xingshi to rescue him and asked Shen Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiuren of Jian'an wanted to send Xingshi to relieve Liu Yu and consulted Shen Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 攸之曰：「孟虯蟻寇，必無能為。

translations.literal: Youzhi said: "Mengjiao is an ant-like foe and surely can accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi said, "Mengjiao is a mere ant — he can do nothing.

sentences.zh: 遣別將馬步數千，足以相制。

translations.literal: Send a separate commander with several thousand horse and foot — that is enough to check him.
translations.idiomatic: A few thousand horse and foot under another commander will be enough.

sentences.zh: 若有意外，且以江西餌之。

translations.literal: If something unexpected occurs, for the moment use Jiangxi as bait for them.
