translations.idiomatic: If something goes wrong, let Jiangxi serve as bait for now.

sentences.zh: 上流若捷，不憂不殄。

translations.literal: If the upper stream is victorious, there is no worry that they will not be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Win upstream and they will be destroyed without fail.

sentences.zh: 興世之行，是安危大機，必不可輟。」

translations.literal: Xingshi's mission is the great hinge of safety and peril and absolutely must not be halted."
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi's mission is the pivot of victory or defeat — it must not be stopped."

sentences.zh: 乃遣段佛榮等援勔。

translations.literal: He then sent Duan Furong and others to aid Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Duan Furong and others to aid Liu Yu instead.

sentences.zh: 興世欲率所領直取大雷，而軍旅未集，不足分張。

translations.literal: Xingshi wished to lead his command straight to take Dalei, but the armies were not yet gathered and there were not enough forces to divide.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi wanted to strike straight at Dalei, but the armies were not yet assembled and he lacked troops to divide.

sentences.zh: 會薛索兒平定，太宗使張永以步騎五千留戍盱眙，餘眾二萬人悉遣南討。

translations.literal: It happened that Xue Suo'er was pacified; Emperor Taizong had Zhang Yong leave five thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison Xuyi and sent the remaining twenty thousand men all south on the punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Suo'er was pacified, the emperor left Zhang Yong with five thousand men at Xuyi and sent the remaining twenty thousand south.

sentences.zh: 山陽又尋平。

translations.literal: Shanyang was soon pacified as well.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang was pacified soon after.

sentences.zh: 徵阮佃夫所領諸軍，悉還南伐，眾軍大集。

translations.literal: The armies led by Ruan Tianfu were summoned back for the southern campaign; the forces gathered in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Tianfu's armies were recalled for the southern campaign, and the hosts assembled in force.

sentences.zh: 乃分戰士七千配興世，興世乃令輕舸泝流而上，旋復回還，一二日中，輒復如此，使賊不為之備。

translations.literal: Seven thousand fighting men were then assigned to Xingshi; Xingshi had light boats go upstream, then turn back again; within a day or two he did this repeatedly, so that the rebels did not prepare against him.
translations.idiomatic: Seven thousand fighters were assigned to Xingshi. He sent light boats upstream, then back again, repeating the feint every day or two until the rebels ceased to guard against him.

sentences.zh: 劉胡聞興世欲上，笑之曰：「我尚不敢越彼下取揚州，張興世何物人，欲輕據我上！」

translations.literal: Liu Hu, hearing that Xingshi wished to go upstream, laughed and said: "I still do not dare to cross below them to take Yangzhou — what sort of man is Zhang Xingshi, that he would lightly seize ground above me!"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Hu heard Xingshi meant to move upstream, he laughed and said, "I would not dare cross below them to take Yangzhou — who is Zhang Xingshi to seize the ground above me!"

sentences.zh: 興世謂攸之等曰：「上流唯有錢谿可據，地既險要，江又甚狹，去大眾不遠，應赴無難。

translations.literal: Xingshi said to Youzhi and others: "Upstream only Qianxi can be held; the ground is strategically vital and the river very narrow; it is not far from the main host, and responding should be without difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi told Youzhi and the others, "Only Qianxi upstream can be held — the ground is vital and the river narrow, close enough to the main army for easy support.

sentences.zh: 江有洄洑，船下必來泊，岸有橫浦，可以藏船舸，二三為宜。」

translations.literal: The river has eddies; boats going downstream must come to moor; the bank has cross channels where boats can be hidden — two or three such places would be suitable."
translations.idiomatic: The river has eddies where downstream boats must moor; cross channels along the bank can hide two or three squadrons."

sentences.zh: 乃夜渡湖口，至鵲頭，因復回下疑之。

translations.literal: He then crossed Hukou by night, reached Quetou, and again turned downstream to make them suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: That night he crossed Hukou to Quetou, then turned downstream again to keep them guessing.

sentences.zh: 其夜四更，值風，仍舉颿直前。

translations.literal: That night at the fourth watch, when wind came, he again raised sail and went straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth watch wind rose, and he set sail straight upstream.

sentences.zh: 賊亦遣胡靈秀諸軍，於東岸相翼而上。

translations.literal: The rebels also sent Hu Lingxiu and other armies winging upward along the eastern bank.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent Hu Lingxiu's force up the eastern bank in support.

sentences.zh: 興世夕住景江浦宿，賊亦不進。

translations.literal: Xingshi in the evening halted at Jingjiang Ford to lodge; the rebels also did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi anchored at Jingjiang Ford that evening; the enemy also halted.

sentences.zh: 夜潛遣黃道摽領七十舸，徑據錢谿，營立城柴。

translations.literal: By night he secretly sent Huang Daobiao leading seventy boats to seize Qianxi directly and encamp, building stockade walls.
translations.idiomatic: By night he secretly sent Huang Daobiao with seventy boats to seize Qianxi and build a stockade.

sentences.zh: 明旦，興世與軍齊集。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day Xingshi and his army gathered together.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Xingshi joined him with the main force.

sentences.zh: 停一宿，劉胡自領水步二十六軍平旦來攻。

translations.literal: After halting one night, Liu Hu personally led twenty-six naval and infantry armies to attack at daybreak.
translations.idiomatic: After one night Liu Hu led twenty-six combined armies against them at dawn.

sentences.zh: 將士欲迎擊之，興世禁曰：「賊來尚遠，而氣盛矢驟，驟既力盡，盛亦易衰，此曹劌之所以破齊也。」

translations.literal: The officers and men wished to go out to meet the attack; Xingshi forbade it, saying: "The rebels are still far off, yet their spirit is high and their arrows fly fast; when the fast attack is spent their strength is exhausted, and when the high spirit is spent it easily declines — this is how Cao Gui defeated Qi."
translations.idiomatic: His men wanted to sally out, but Xingshi forbade it: "The enemy is still far, but their fury is at its peak. Let them spend it — that is how Cao Gui beat Qi."

sentences.zh: 令將士不得妄動，治城如故。

translations.literal: He ordered the officers and men not to move rashly and to continue fortifying the camp as before.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his men to hold their positions and keep building the fortifications.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊來轉近，舫入洄洑，興世乃命壽寂之、任農夫率壯士數百擊之，眾軍相繼進，胡於是敗走。

translations.literal: Soon the rebels drew nearer; their boats entered the eddies; Xingshi then ordered Shou Jizhi and Ren Nongfu to lead several hundred stalwarts to strike them; the armies followed in succession, and Hu thereupon was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: As the enemy drew near and their boats entered the eddies, Xingshi sent Shou Jizhi and Ren Nongfu with hundreds of picked men to strike; the rest followed, and Liu Hu fled.

sentences.zh: 斬級數百，投水者甚眾，胡收軍而下。

translations.literal: Several hundred heads were cut; very many cast themselves into the water; Hu gathered his army and withdrew downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds were beheaded and many drowned; Hu gathered what remained and withdrew downstream.

sentences.zh: 時興世城壘未固，司徒建安王休仁慮賊并力更攻錢谿，欲分其形勢，命沈攸之、吳喜、佼長生、劉靈遺等以皮艦二十，攻賊濃湖，苦戰連日，斬獲千數。

translations.literal: At that time Xingshi's fortifications were not yet solid; the Minister of Works, Prince of Jian'an, Xiuren, fearing the rebels would combine forces to attack Qianxi again, wished to divide their strength and ordered Shen Youzhi, Wu Xi, Jiao Changsheng, Liu Lingyi, and others with twenty leather warships to attack the rebels' Nonghu, fighting bitterly for many days and beheading and capturing by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: While Xingshi's fort was still unfinished, Prince Xiuren of Jian'an feared a combined assault on Qianxi and ordered Shen Youzhi, Wu Xi, and others with twenty warships to attack Nonghu, fighting bitterly for days and taking thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 是日，劉胡果率眾軍，欲更攻興世。

translations.literal: That same day Liu Hu indeed led the mass of armies, intending to attack Xingshi again.
translations.idiomatic: That day Liu Hu did lead his armies to attack Xingshi again.

sentences.zh: 未至錢谿數十里，袁顗以濃湖之急遽追之，錢谿城柴由此得立。

translations.literal: When he was still several tens of li from Qianxi, Yuan Yi, because of the urgency at Nonghu, hurriedly recalled him; the stockade at Qianxi was thereby able to stand firm.
translations.idiomatic: When he was still tens of li from Qianxi, Yuan Yi recalled him urgently because of the crisis at Nonghu, and the Qianxi stockade was completed.

sentences.zh: 賊連戰轉敗，興世又遏其糧道，尋陽遣運至南陵，不敢下，賊眾漸饑。

translations.literal: The rebels were defeated in battle after battle; Xingshi also blocked their grain route; Xunyang sent transport to Nanling but dared not land; the rebel host gradually grew hungry.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels lost battle after battle. Xingshi blocked their grain route; convoys from Xunyang reached Nanling but dared not land, and hunger spread through the rebel ranks.

sentences.zh: 劉胡乃遣顗安北府司馬、偽右軍沈仲玉領千人步取南陵，迎接糧運。

translations.literal: Liu Hu then sent Yi's Pacify-the-North headquarters Major, the false Right Army commander Shen Zhongyu, leading a thousand infantry to take Nanling and meet the grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu sent Yuan Yi's staff officer Shen Zhongyu with a thousand foot soldiers to seize Nanling and escort the grain convoy.

sentences.zh: 仲玉至南陵，領米三十萬斛，錢布數十舫，豎榜為城，規欲突過。

translations.literal: Zhongyu reached Nanling, took charge of three hundred thousand hu of grain and several tens of boats of cash and cloth, set up placards as a wall, and planned to break through in a rush.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanling Zhongyu took charge of three hundred thousand hu of grain and dozens of boats of cash and cloth, raised barricades like a wall, and prepared to force a passage downstream.

sentences.zh: 行至貴口，不敢進，遣間信報胡，令遣重軍援接。

translations.literal: When he reached Guikou he did not dare advance and sent a secret messenger to report to Hu, asking him to send a heavy force to support and meet him.
translations.idiomatic: At Guikou he halted, too afraid to advance, and sent a secret messenger asking Liu Hu for a strong escort.

sentences.zh: 興世、壽寂之、任農夫、李安民等三千人至貴口擊之，與仲玉相值。

translations.literal: Xingshi, Shou Jizhi, Ren Nongfu, Li Anmin, and others with three thousand men reached Guikou to attack him and encountered Zhongyu.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi, Shou Jizhi, Ren Nongfu, and Li Anmin with three thousand men struck at Guikou and met Zhongyu.

sentences.zh: 交戰盡日，仲玉走還顗營，悉虜其資實；

translations.literal: They fought all day; Zhongyu fled back to Yi's camp; all his supplies and goods were captured;
translations.idiomatic: They fought all day. Zhongyu fled to Yuan Yi's camp and left all his stores behind;

sentences.zh: 賊眾大敗，胡棄軍遁走，顗仍亦奔散。

translations.literal: the rebel host was greatly defeated; Hu abandoned his army and fled; Yi also broke and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: the rebel army was shattered. Liu Hu abandoned his troops and fled; Yuan Yi broke and scattered as well.

sentences.zh: 興世率軍追討，與吳喜共平江陵。

translations.literal: Xingshi led his army in pursuit and, together with Wu Xi, pacified Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi pursued the enemy and, with Wu Xi, pacified Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 遷左軍將軍，尋為督豫、司二州、南豫州之梁郡諸軍事，封作唐縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was moved to General of the Left Army, soon made Commander over the military affairs of Yu and Si provinces and Liang commandery of Southern Yu, enfeoffed as Marquis of Zuotang county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He became General of the Left Army, then commander over Yu and Si and Liang in southern Yu, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zuotang with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 徵為游擊將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as General of Mobile Strikes.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as General of Mobile Strikes.

sentences.zh: 興世居臨沔水，沔水自襄陽以下，至於九江，二千里中，先無洲嶼。

translations.literal: Xingshi's residence faced the Mian River; from Xiangyang downstream to Jiujiang, within two thousand li there had formerly been no islets or sandbanks.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi lived on the Mian River. From Xiangyang to Jiujiang — two thousand li of water — there had never been an islet.

sentences.zh: 興世初生，當其門前水中，一旦忽生洲，年年漸大，及至興世為方伯，而洲上遂十餘頃。

translations.literal: When Xingshi was newly born, in the water before his gate an islet suddenly appeared one day; year by year it gradually grew larger, and by the time Xingshi became a regional commander the islet had reached more than ten qing.
translations.idiomatic: When he was born, an islet suddenly rose in the water before his gate. It grew year by year until, when he became a regional commander, it covered more than ten qing.

sentences.zh: 父仲子，由興世致位給事中。

translations.literal: His father Zhongzi, through Xingshi's attainment of rank, became a Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongzi rose to palace attendant through Xingshi's success.

sentences.zh: 興世欲將往襄陽，愛戀鄉里，不肯去。

translations.literal: Xingshi wished to take him to Xiangyang, but he loved his native place and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingshi wanted to take him to Xiangyang, he refused to leave his home village.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂興世：「我雖田舍老公，樂聞鼓角，可送一部，行田時吹之。」

translations.literal: He once said to Xingshi: "Though I am an old farmer, I delight in hearing drums and horns — you could send me a set to blow when I walk the fields."
translations.idiomatic: He once told Xingshi, "I may be a rustic old man, but I love the sound of drums and horns. Send me a set to play when I walk the fields."

sentences.zh: 興世素恭謹畏法憲，譬之曰：「此是天子鼓角，非田舍老公所吹。」

translations.literal: Xingshi, who was always respectful, cautious, and in awe of law and statute, answered him: "Those are the Son of Heaven's drums and horns — not for an old farmer to blow."
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi, ever respectful of law, replied, "Those are the Son of Heaven's drums and horns — not for a rustic old man to blow."

sentences.zh: 興世欲拜墓，仲子謂曰：「汝衛從太多，先人必當驚怖。」

translations.literal: When Xingshi wished to pay respects at the tombs, Zhongzi said to him: "Your escort is too large — our forebears would surely be startled and afraid."
translations.idiomatic: When Xingshi planned to visit the family graves, Zhongzi said, "Your escort is too large — our ancestors would be terrified."

sentences.zh: 興世減撤而後行。

translations.literal: Xingshi reduced and withdrew escort before he went.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi reduced his escort before he went.

sentences.zh: 興世子欣業，當嗣封，會齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: Xingshi's son Xinye was to inherit the enfeoffment; it happened that Qi received the abdication and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi's son Xinye was to inherit the title, but when Qi took the throne the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：兵固詭道，勝在用奇。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: War is indeed the way of deception; victory lies in using the strange.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: War is deception, and victory belongs to the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 當二帝爭雄，天人之分未決，南北連兵，相阨而不得進者，半歲矣。

translations.literal: When the two emperors contended for supremacy and the division between Heaven and man was not yet decided, north and south linked arms in battle and blocked each other unable to advance — for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: When two emperors contended and the mandate of Heaven hung in the balance, the armies of north and south faced each other without moving for half a year.

sentences.zh: 蓋乃趙壁拔幟之機，官渡熸師之日，至於鵲浦投戈，實興世用奇之力也。

translations.literal: It was like the moment when banners were pulled from the Zhao wall, the day when armies were extinguished at Guandu — as for the casting down of weapons at Quepu, that was truly the power of Xingshi's use of the strange.
translations.idiomatic: It was a moment like pulling the Zhao banners from the wall, like the annihilation at Guandu — and the casting down of arms at Quepu was truly the work of Xingshi's stratagem.

sentences.zh: 建斾垂組，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: To raise banners and let ribbons hang — was that for nothing!
translations.idiomatic: His banners and ribbons were not won in vain!
